newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: INTERVIEW - BAESA seeks capital injection - CEO.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BAESA seeks capital injection - CEO.

text.p: Argentina's Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (BAESA) is seeking fresh capital and is considering taking on a new partner or selling assets, its President and CEO Luis Suarez said Wednesday.

"BAESA is looking to strengthen its capital structure," he told Reuters in a phone interview. Asked whether that implied the incorporation of a new partner or sales of non-strategic assets or operations he said: "All options are open. Our objective is to maximize value."
Suarez said the main challenge for BAESA, the biggest PepsiCo Inc bottler outside the United States, was to discuss with creditor banks a new plan to restructure debt of about $800 million.

"In the coming days will will submit to our creditors a proposal to restructure debts, consisting basically of a restructuring of principal and new conditions. We are discussing all options with them. Maybe the main point is a new capital injection."

On announcing Tuesday first quarter results, Suarez had said a 100-day plan launched in July 1996 was fruitful in reversing the operational difficulties that generated great losses, basically due to BAESA's performance in Brazil.
Many analysts blame Brazilian operations, which they feel were overexpanded in 1995, as the main reason behind the company's troubles.

Asked whether BAESA could spin off non-strategic assets or operations in Brazil, Suarez said, "I think the worst in Brazil is over. We have restructured the company there to practically the size it should have had."
The restructuring of Brazilian operations involved hundreds of layoffs and the closing of utilities.

BAESA has the exclusive Pepsi and Seven-Up franchises for the Buenos Aires metropolitan area and other regions in Argentina, as well as Chile, Uruguay and Costa Rica and certain Southern Brazilian states, including the metropolitan areas of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.

Suarez said last year's agreement with creditors to defer until March 31 repayments of capital of about $520 million in debts together with $40 million in financial and marketing support from PepsiCo, gave BAESA the necessary time and resources to improve operating performance.
Asked whether the firm was considering asking additional help from PepsiCo, which has operating control over BAESA, he said it was too early to tell but "all options are open."
In fiscal 1996 BAESA lost $452.4 million versus a $44.8 million profit in 1995.
On Tuesday it announced a reduction in first quarter net losses to $16.7 million from $22.9 million in the same period of the previous year.
Suarez said those results were encouraging and a sign that "we are on the right way."
However, he struck a very cautious note, saying "There are no celebrations. We don't think the game is over. We have to streghthen the company as the situation is every time harder."
"We are still worried. Looking where to reduce costs. With PepsiCo's support we are launching in Argentina and Brazil a more agressive marketing drive."
"We are in an economy of war." ((--Buenos Aires Newsroom, 541 318-0650)
